analysis:
Integration review of the desktop per-chip earnings recommendation change. Replayed source covers recommendations.ts (chipEarnings/chipRanking/recommendedModels), contracts.ts types, StartServing.tsx, AutopilotModels.tsx, RecommendedModels.tsx, the test fixture, changelog and docs. The change is renderer-only plus type and docs updates. It does not touch the provider process, the coordinator WebSocket contract (TB-002), keys (A-002/A-003), attestation or App Attest authorization (TB-009/TB-011), the prefix cache (T-041) or the fan helper.

Verified directly in recommendations.ts:
- chipEarnings requires fresh network earnings (via networkEarnings), by_chip_window === '24h', an Array by_chip, a safe-integer machines count of at least 1, and digit-only amount strings before any BigInt call. Malformed input returns null, so BigInt cannot throw on untrusted coordinator data. Output falls back to network totals.
- The perChip branch of recommendedModels filters on model.eligible (set locally by the runtime) and on mean > 0n, so the non-null assertions in the sort are safe.
- chipRanking falls back to network totals when per-chip data recommends no servable model.
- Rendering uses React text interpolation, so there is no XSS vector. The chip string comes from the local snapshot.
- The worst case is a compromised or hostile stats source skewing which already-eligible models are recommended. That was already possible with the 7-day totals. Serving authorization and admission remain coordinator/platform-owned, and the Swift side re-validates the catalog and pin capacity per the docs.

Residual unverified items, not findings: the Swift DesktopBackend.resource relay of /v1/stats (size bounds and 'relayed unchanged') was not supplied, and the coordinator's by_chip publication contract is out of scope. The display mixes 7d and 24h windows, which is a presentation concern only. 34 replay units were omitted, and some were presumably tests. No security regression was identified.
